memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the cover. Place the cover on top of the ark and put in the ark the tablets of the covenant law that I will give you. There, above the cover between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the covenant law, I will meet with you and give you all my commands for the Israelites." - Exodus 25:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God names the exact place where He will meet with His people: above the mercy seat, between the cherubim. Of all the places He could have chosen, God chose to meet at the place of atonement. Not at the place of the law's demands, but at the place where mercy covered them. The meeting point between God and sinners has always been the place of grace.

The cherubim gaze down toward the cover, as if even the angels are fascinated by what happens there. Peter writes that angels long to look into these things — the sufferings of Christ and the glory that followed (1 Pet 1:12). Heaven itself leans in to watch God's mercy at work.

And notice God's words: "I will meet with you." God did not merely accept sacrifices; He wanted conversation, communion, relationship. The whole elaborate structure existed so that God and His people could meet. Today, that meeting place is a Person. Jesus is where God and humanity come together, and through Him we approach the throne of grace with confidence (Heb 4:16). You do not need a tent, a lid of gold, or a priest with blood. You have Christ. Come and meet with God today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I approach God at the place of mercy rather than trying to earn my way?
Am I making time to actually meet with God, not just know about Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You desire to meet with me, and that in Christ the way is fully open. Draw me to the throne of grace today, and speak to my listening heart. Amen.
